name: batch-10
prompt:
Create ONE production game-icon SPRITE ATLAS, exactly 3 columns by 3 rows on a square canvas, ideally 2048x2048, genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha PNG. Input image is the user's approved style sheet, STYLE reference only. Match that soft tactile dimensional 3D collectible family: gentle warm upper-left diffuse studio light, rounded yet faithful forms, bright pastel/candy color, subtle ambient occlusion, restrained material detail. Each object's true material remains recognizable: paper, wood, glass, metal, woven cloth. No same-clay treatment on everything. No heavy dark outlines or flat vector art.

CRITICAL PACKAGING: There are EXACTLY NINE equal square virtual cells in a regular 3x3 grid. Draw ONE specified object/group centered within EACH virtual cell, at ONLY 48–52% of cell width/height, with at least 24% EMPTY TRANSPARENT MARGIN ON EVERY SIDE. Nothing may touch a virtual cell edge or cross into a neighbor. All strings, handles, leaves and shadows stay inside their own cell. Think SMALL MINIATURE ICONS with LARGE EMPTY GUTTERS, NOT large illustrations filling the sheet. Icon centers are x=16.67%,50%,83.33%, y=16.67%,50%,83.33% of the image. Each icon must fit in a box 18% of the overall image size. Empty space between shapes is essential. No visible grid lines, no backgrounds, no color squares, no borders, no captions, numbers, words, ID labels, titles or decorative props. Empty padding is genuine alpha transparency, NOT a drawn checkerboard. Top-left through bottom-right order is mandatory; do not swap cells. Each tile will be cropped at exact one-third boundaries into a separate icon. Keep centered and similarly weighted, readable at 32–66px. All objects fully in frame, no cropping. Only allow inscription glyphs explicitly specified in subject. Do not invent sacred symbols, cultural ornament, claims or text. No extra humans/hands/landscape/pedestals. Subject list in strict row-major order:
1. Cell row 1, column 1: A vermilion wooden torii gate with two upright pillars, a horizontal lower crossbeam and a broad gently upswept upper lintel with a dark-brown cap; short dark pillar footings, with no rope, plaque or added crest.
2. Cell row 1, column 2: One fixed upright prayer drum on a vertical axle between two tan wooden horizontal supports; the short red cylindrical shell has gold top and bottom bands, a golden elliptical lid and three small gold studs, without script or a handheld chain.
3. Cell row 1, column 3: One light sakura-pink origami paper crane with a small bent beak and long folded neck pointing left, a sharp tail extending right, two raised triangular wings and a compact diamond-shaped body; preserve crisp folds, thin paper edges and the original open silhouette.
4. Cell row 2, column 1: A green woven-stem flower wreath with an open center, six simple coral, yellow, blue, ivory and pink blossoms, two coral ribbon tails and the existing icon's small cream candle with a warm flame inside the ring.
5. Cell row 2, column 2: A red rounded wooden daruma head with a cream face above three thick wooden discs in red, muted teal and ochre, the lowest disc offset to the right. A small natural-wood mallet stands alongside; keep the separate stacked pieces visible.
6. Cell row 2, column 3: A four-wing folded-paper pinwheel with alternating coral and turquoise blades, a small pale-gold axle bead and a straight warm-brown wooden stick. Keep exactly four curled triangular paper wings meeting at one central pin.
7. Cell row 3, column 1: A slender brown wooden steelyard beam with a small lifting ring, a brass-colored pan suspended from cords at the left and a dark metal sliding weight at the right. One orange fruit rests in the shallow pan; preserve the off-center balance structure.
8. Cell row 3, column 2: A natural-wood long-handled croquet mallet beside one coral-red ball with a cream stripe and a pale grey metal U-shaped wicket on a short green ground strip. Keep the open wicket and horizontal cylindrical mallet head distinct.
9. Cell row 3, column 3: A vertical honey-brown wooden drop spindle with a broad circular whorl low on its shaft and a compact cream yarn cop wound above the whorl. A small pale wool tuft and fine thread sit at the top; preserve the low-whorl structure.
